title: The Lamp in the Cellar
author: Told in the Green Combes
pages: Once there was a big house called the World, and under the World there was a cellar, and in the cellar there was a lamp. The lamp was old and grumpy and very hot, and nobody liked going down there.
But the lamp kept the cellar from flooding with dark, and the dark down there was the hungry kind. So once in a long while somebody brave went down and trimmed the wick and came back up shaking.
One year a clever person said: that lamp is a nuisance and it bites. Let us put it out. So they went down with a big stick and put it out. And the dark came up the stairs, and that was a bad winter.
So what do you do, little ones, when the lamp is out? You shut the door and keep the kettle on. You count the jars. You light every candle. And you send someone brave to find a new wick.
And what does the brave one have to pay, Gran? Hush now. Something they love. That's the way of lamps. Off to bed, and leave a light on.
